bull_bear.body:
- Asset-light tilt: outsourcing commodity sheet-metal (Flamecraft), JV-funding backward integration (Tricoree, 34% — minimal cash so far) to protect proprietary chimney know-how.
- Reinvesting in capacity (Panchkula) + automation + new product lines.
- No buyback/dividend detail given; promoter stake increase / equity raise = "consider after Diwali"; SME→main-board migration pending eligibility.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Demand cyclicality / Gulf sensitivity:** Q4 collapse (expected INR 55-60 cr → actual ~INR 35-37 cr) shows end-demand is volatile and tied to Middle-East sentiment.
- **RM / FX exposure:** weak INR + RMB strength + commodity inflation; pass-through incomplete → H1 FY27 margin pressure acknowledged.
- **China dependency:** electronics, switches, BLDC motors, heat elements (~INR 150-170 each) still imported; BIS on motors not yet in (a risk and an opportunity).
- **Execution / new-product ramp:** built-in microwaves/dishwashers depend on training fresh workforce; mgmt deliberately "not putting pressure" in FY27 → revenue mix shift may be back-end loaded.
- **Governance/visibility:** no formal order book; refused several forward-looking questions; SME-board liquidity; stock price weak (mgmt deflected).
- **JV opacity:** Tricoree details withheld ("not appropriate time to disclose").
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Amit Kaushik is candid, operator-minded and detail-rich on manufacturing/technology; openly owned the Q4 miss and margin squeeze. Strong import-substitution / "Make in India" conviction and clear de-risking logic (own the glass, motor, electronics; outsource sheet-metal). Notably dismissive of stock-price questions ("My work is to work... don't put pressure on me for stock price"). Some promotional framing on the built-in "monopoly" and INR 500 cr aspiration; forward financials kept vague (percentages, not absolutes).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The investable angle is China+1 / BIS-driven localisation: each BIS notification (chimneys done; hobs ~Sep-2026; possibly motors next) converts an imported category into a domestic-assembly opportunity where Inflame claims first-mover/sole-maker status on several built-in products.
- Backward integration (BLDC motors + PCB via 34% Tricoree) is the margin and de-risk lever, but it is ~2-2.5 years out and currently raises near-term China RM dependency as BLDC mix climbs.
- FY27 is explicitly a "preparation year" — growth comes from chimneys; built-in products are being lined up for FY28+ — so the mix-shift / INR 500 cr story is back-end loaded and execution/training-dependent.
- Operating-leverage claim (fixed manpower to ~INR 350 cr) means margins should expand sharply if the 50% growth lands — the key thing to verify next quarter.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **Chimneys (core, ~60-65% target mix):** 270k units FY26; largest BLDC-chimney OEM in India; ~60% of production already BLDC, targeting ~80% by FY27-end. Complaint ratio <1.5% (vs much higher for Chinese product); 10-year motor warranties. BIS on chimneys fully implemented (CKD/SKD imports now hard).
- **Built-in / value-added (Hyderabad plant):** built-in refrigerators (ASP ~INR 38-40k) and wine coolers (~INR 30-35k) — both "completely ready"; built-in ovens ramping (2-3 weeks); dishwashers & built-in microwaves (~INR 15-22k) to be production-ready by Dec-Jan, full readiness Apr-2027. ~1,000 cooling units made to date. "No other company makes these" — claimed USP/monopoly in India.
- **Flamecraft (51%):** Hyderabad sheet-metal — strategy is to outsource non-core sheet-metal, keep difficult/assembly processes in-house.
- **Tricoree Machmatrix (34%, newly incorporated):** BLDC motors (phase 1), electronics/PCB & switches (phase 2), then IoT/smart-control. No cash investment yet beyond formation; built on partners' machines/land.

latest_quarter.body:
- RM is the largest cost; RM consumption rose H1 ~70% → H2 ~75% of sales, mostly in Q4. FX (weak INR) alone ~INR 70-80 lakh hit; Yuan/RMB appreciation lifted Chinese supplier prices.
- Pass-through partial (not 100%) — offset via efficiency, alternate materials, alternate suppliers, AI-QC output gains.
- Operating leverage thesis: manpower ~fixed up to ~INR 350 cr revenue; R&D/tech spend already booked → incremental EBITDA flows through. Historically recovered from 15-16% to 30% gross margin after a prior ~100% RM spike.
- BLDC mix rising raises China RM dependency near-term (~37-38% of BLDC-motor input from China) — backward integration is the structural fix.
- Inventory elevated because built-in products (refs, ovens, hobs) imported in CKD/SKD; ~40-50% of inventory to unwind once motors/PCBs made in India (JIT).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 / H2 FY26 (this):** FY26 revenue +41-42%, EBITDA +~55%, EPS +~85%; 270k chimneys (+38%); but soft Q4 (vol +20%, rev +11%, ~INR 35-37 cr vs INR 55-60 cr expected) on RM inflation + weak INR + Gulf-conflict demand drop + gas-supply disruption. Incorporated Tricoree Machmatrix (34%) for BLDC/electronics backward integration; Panchkula INR 8-10 cr expansion phasing in (ground floor live, floors 2-3 by Aug/Sep). Guidance: ~50% growth FY27, 4 lakh chimneys, INR 400 cr+ FY28 / INR 500 cr FY28-29; chimney mix to fall to ~60-65%.
- _Next Q → check: (1) H1 FY27 margin (RM pass-through complete? AI-QC output gains?); (2) ~50% growth / 4-lakh-chimney run-rate on track; (3) Panchkula floors 2-3 commissioned on time (Aug/Sep); (4) hobs BIS finalised ~Sep-2026; (5) built-in product ramp (ovens, then dishwashers/microwaves by Dec-Jan); (6) Tricoree BLDC-motor progress; (7) any SME→main-board / equity-raise move post-Diwali._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** ~45-50% in FY27 (units & revenue); already "on track" two months in.
- **Volume:** 4 lakh chimneys targeted in FY27 (vs 270k FY26); long-run aspiration ~6 lakh chimneys before pushing exports.
- **Revenue milestones:** INR 400 cr+ in FY28; INR 500 cr in FY28-29.
- **Mix shift:** chimneys to fall to ~60-65% of revenue as built-in products (ovens, refs, wine coolers, hobs, dishwashers, microwaves) scale; "other products" to rise from ~5-10% toward 15-20%.
- **Margin:** even if % dips slightly on RM, absolute EBITDA/PAT to rise with the topline (manpower largely fixed up to ~INR 150-350 cr revenue — operating leverage). AI camera-vision QC to lift output ~15-20%.
- **Capex / commissioning:** INR 8-10 cr Panchkula expansion (50,000 sq ft, 3 floors) — ground floor live in ~2-3 days (+12-15k chimney capacity); 2nd floor by ~15-Aug; 3rd floor by ~30-Sep.
- **Backward integration:** BLDC motors ~1-1.5 yrs out; electronics/PCB a further ~1-1.5 yrs (so ~2-2.5 yrs to in-house components) via Tricoree Machmatrix (34%).
- **Regulatory:** hobs BIS expected to be finalised ~Sep 2026 (postponed twice).

- No formal multi-month order book — customers give firm monthly schedules only; Inflame plans off known model-wise share (Hindware ~40 models, KAFF ~18-20, Havells ~12). India OEM "pressure" exceeds planned growth.
- Key OEM customers: Havells (business grown multi-fold — "pressure to supply more"), Hindware (back on track after ~1-1.5 yr management-change disruption), IFB, Crompton, KAFF. All major buyers were "short of orders" in soft Q4.

outlook.body:
- **Premiumisation / new-product ladder:** built-in appliances are higher-ASP and currently un-contested in India (import-substitution moat).
- **Backward integration:** in-house BLDC motors + PCB/electronics → margin uplift + China de-risk + potential external BLDC-motor sales into a shortage market.
- **Automation:** AI camera-vision quality control (Mumbai partner) to cut inspection time and lift output ~15-20%; potential zero-manpower glass plant once revenue crosses INR 250-300 cr.
- **Exports:** inquiries received; deferred until domestic OEM demand (~6 lakh chimneys) is saturated.
- **Main-board migration:** currently BSE-SME; blocked by paid-up capital <INR 10 cr and net worth <INR 75 cr — will migrate once eligible; possible equity raise / promoter stake increase considered post-Diwali.

deepdive.thesis: Inflame is a Panchkula-based OEM/ODM kitchen-appliance maker (India's largest BLDC-chimney OEM) that grew FY26 revenue ~41-42% with EBITDA up ~55% and EPS up ~85%, but hit a soft, RM-inflation-squeezed Q4 (vol +20%, rev only +11%) as Gulf-conflict demand jitters and a weak rupee bit before prices could be passed through. The real story is a deliberate China+1 / import-substitution build-out — using BIS-driven localisation to add high-ASP built-in products (refrigerators, wine coolers, ovens, dishwashers, microwaves, hobs) and to backward-integrate BLDC motors + PCBs via a 34%-owned JV — targeting ~50% growth in FY27 and INR 500 cr revenue by FY28-29.

one-line thesis: A BSE-SME chimney-OEM that grew ~41–42% in FY26 with 55% EBITDA growth, now leveraging entrenched BIS-driven import-substitution to add high-ASP built-in appliances and backward-integrate into BLDC motors/PCB — guiding ~50% revenue growth in FY27 toward INR400cr+ by FY28 and INR500cr by FY28–29, but with near-term margin pressure from RM/FX and unproven new-product ramp.
financial scorecard: (Note: SME, half-yearly reporting; no precise rupee P&L given on call — figures are management commentary / qualitative.)
Revenue (FY26): grew ~41–42% YoY (implied base ~INR135–150cr → FY26 likely ~INR190–210cr; mgmt referenced "INR150cr / INR250cr / INR350cr" cost-structure bands, not exact rev). EPS up ~85% YoY.
EBITDA: grew ~55% YoY → higher EBITDA margin and higher PAT (directional; no absolute figure).

Gross margin: under pressure in H2/Q4. RM consumed rose 70%→75% of sales H1→H2 (commodity inflation + INR depreciation). FX alone cost ~INR70–80 lakh. Historically improved 15–16% → 30% gross margin in a prior RM-spike cycle.

Q4FY26 (weak): chimney volume +20% YoY but revenue +11% YoY only. Management expected ~INR55–60cr quarter; actual ~INR35–37cr. Cause: soft Gulf/geopolitical demand + RM/FX cost spike + 3-week gas-supply disruption.
Chimney volumes: 270,000 units FY26 vs 195,000 FY25 (+38%). Capacity utilization ~50% across both plants. Hyderabad +31%, Panchkula +42% growth.
Order book: no firm rupee number — customers give 1-month firm schedules; mgmt says order position "more than the growth we are planning." Complaint ratio <1.5% (vs China much higher).

Cash/net debt: not disclosed. Inventory flagged as high (by analyst) — mgmt: due to carrying China-imported SKD/CKD for hobs/refs/ovens; expected to drop 40–50% once motors/PCB made in India (just-in-time).
One-offs: Q4 hit by gas-procurement disruption (~3 weeks) and Middle-East-driven RM spike; price pass-through was lagging (started post-March, ~1.5–2 months to complete).
guidance (critical): Revenue growth FY27: targeting ~50% YoY ("two months in, on track"); INR200–225cr range implied.
Medium-term: INR400cr+ by FY28 ("for sure"); INR500cr by FY28–FY29.
Chimney volume: targeting 4 lakh (400,000) chimneys in FY27 (vs 270k FY26) — i.e. ~50% growth; aspiration to sustain India OEM up to 6 lakh chimneys before pushing exports.

Margin guidance: near-term pressure acknowledged ("already pressure on margin"); mgmt expects to absorb RM/FX via efficiency, alternate material/suppliers, RMB LC sourcing, and AI visual-inspection (claims 15–20% output/inspection-time gain). Guides margins/EBITDA to rise with scale (manpower largely fixed up to INR350cr). Even if margin slips a couple of pts, absolute PAT to grow.

New products: built-in refrigerator & wine coolers "completely ready"; built-in ovens ramping in 2–3 weeks; dishwasher + built-in microwave to be set by Dec–Jan; aim to be ready to supply "any number" from Apr-2027. FY27 growth driven by chimney; FY28 growth from chimney + new products.
Mix shift: chimney share to fall to ~60–65% of revenue going forward (from ~85–90%) as built-ins scale.
order book & pipeline: Key OEM customers: IFB, Crompton, Hindware, Havells, KAFF. All were short of orders in Q4 (demand-driven, not share loss).
Havells business "grown multi-fold" — now pressure to supply more.
Hindware back on track after 1–1.5 yrs of disruption (their key-management churn) — order book "very good now."
Models are customer-locked (e.g. ~40 models Hindware, ~12 Havells, ~18–20 KAFF) and not made by other suppliers → sticky, single-source positioning.
Indicative monthly pulls: Hindware ~10,000; Havells ~5,000–10,000; KAFF ~6,000–7,000 chimneys.
USP: built-in microwave/dishwasher/ovens "not made by any other company" in India — "no one is doing it, go to Inflame."
segment / subsidiary detail: Panchkula plant (Haryana): mass + premium chimneys; +42% growth; site of INR8–10cr capex expansion.
Hyderabad plant: value-added / new products (built-in ovens, wine coolers, refrigerators developed here); +31%; deliberately NOT run for high utilization — positioned as exclusive/value-added line.
Flamecraft (Hyderabad): sheet-metal sub, Inflame holds 51% — strategy to push non-core sheet-metal processes out of main factory and keep focus on assembly + hard-to-replicate processes.
Tricoree Machmatrix Pvt Ltd (associate, 34%): new — BLDC motors (phase 1), then electronics/PCB/switches (phase 2), then IoT/smart-control (phase 3). See §6.
growth verticals / optionality: Built-in appliances (high ASP): built-in fridge ASP ~INR38–40k; wine cooler ~INR30–35k; built-in microwave/dishwasher ~INR15–22k. At 50 units/day of fridges, ~INR50–70cr revenue potential. Currently ~14–15 combined pieces/day. Demand pull from buyers strong; Galanz (China) director visiting Hyderabad to discuss supply chain; Midea referenced.

Backward integration (Tricoree): BLDC motors first (37–38% of motor RMC from China today; 60% of production now BLDC, heading to 70–80%). Inflame is "largest BLDC-chimney producer in OEM sector." Goal: "ruling BLDC market in India" in 2–2.5 yrs. PCB/switches next. NOTE: no capital invested yet in Tricoree beyond forming the company — mgmt vague, says full disclosure "at the appropriate time" via exchange.
Hob/cooktop: BIS expected Sep-2026 → import substitution kicker; currently still imported from China (CKD/SKD).
Exports: inquiries received; deferred until India OEM demand (~6 lakh chimneys) is satisfied.
Glass plant (future): zero-manpower, +250% productivity, but capital-heavy — only after crossing INR250–300cr.
margins & cost dynamics: RM is largest cost, then manpower (manpower roughly fixed up to INR150–350cr revenue) → operating leverage thesis.
H2/Q4 squeezed by: commodity inflation, INR depreciation (FX cost ~INR70–80 lakh), RMB/Yuan appreciation raising Chinese-supplier prices, RM consumption 70%→75%.

Mitigations: pass-through (partial, not 100%, ~1.5–2 months to complete), alternate materials/suppliers, opening LCs in RMB (started May), AI visual-inspection cutting inspection time (claims 10–20% of time → output gain), automation of critical processes.
Mgmt confident of stable-to-improving margins on scale; "we will absorb everything."
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Panchkula INR8–10cr expansion: 50,000 sq ft new construction in 3 parts.
Part 1 (ground floor): ready, operational "in next 2–3 days" → adds 12,000–15,000 chimneys capacity.
→ Slippage risk flagged: only 1 of 3 parts done at call date; full benefit phased through H2FY27.
Automation/AI inspection capex ongoing (~1.5 yrs running).
Tricoree plant being set up (land + machines) by partners — Inflame's direct cash outlay minimal so far.
capital allocation: Promoter stake raise: "will consider," but unlikely in short run — possibly post-Diwali (signals promoter view stock undervalued).

Main-board migration (from BSE SME): currently ineligible — needs min INR10cr paid-up capital and INR75cr net worth; mgmt says "from here on we will be eligible" and will work on it. Equity-raise to enable migration is a forward-looking open question (not committed).
Capital deployed into capacity (Panchkula), subs (Flamecraft 51%) and associate (Tricoree 34%) — backward-integration-led allocation.
Mgmt deflected stock-price questions ("my work is to work / put pressure on me for performance, not stock price").
risks & watch-items: Customer concentration: revenue tied to 5 OEMs (IFB, Crompton, Hindware, Havells, KAFF); Q4 showed all going soft simultaneously → demand correlated.

China import dependency: electronics, switches, BLDC motors, heating elements (~INR150–170/unit), and 80–100% of components for new built-in products imported from China; FX/RMB volatility hits margins directly.
Margin/FX risk: RM 75% of sales, partial pass-through, INR weakness.
New-product execution: built-in microwave/dishwasher/ovens at "inception stage"; ramp depends on training fresh workforce; ASP-rich but low current volume.
Tricoree opacity: backward-integration JV undisclosed in detail, no capital committed yet, 2–2.5 yr horizon — execution & disclosure risk.
BIS timing risk: hobs BIS already postponed twice; now expected Sep-2026 — slippage delays the import-substitution tailwind.
Capacity slippage: Aug/Sep-2026 plant parts could slip.
SME liquidity / governance optics: still on BSE SME, low float, no firm migration timeline.
management quality / tone: Candid and operationally detailed (named customers, volumes, ASPs, RM%, plant timelines). Owner-operator (Kaushik family) deeply hands-on in tech/process.
Honest about Q4 miss (admitted expected INR55–60cr came in at ~INR35–37cr) and partial pass-through ("not 100%, if I tell you the truth").
Some evasiveness on Tricoree specifics, main-board timing, and equity raise — deferred to "appropriate time."
Confident, growth-focused; refused to engage on stock price. Overall credible, execution-oriented, but guidance is ambitious vs SME scale.
non-obvious takeaways: The Tricoree (34%) BLDC-motor associate is a regulatory-arbitrage hedge: mgmt is pre-positioning for a possible future BIS on BLDC motors — if it lands, Inflame controls supply and locks out competitors; if not, optional upside in selling motors to other appliance makers.
34% stake (vs control) is deliberate — keeps chimney-motor IP captive ("no competitor should take its benefit") while sharing capital/risk with two motor/PCB experts.
Built-in appliances are a moat-by-tedium play: market too small for others to set up (~500 pcs viability) → Inflame becomes default single supplier ("go to Inflame").
Hyderabad's "low utilization" is intentional positioning, not a problem — reframed as a premium/NPD lab.
Inventory bloat is a feature of import-substitution transition (carrying China SKD/CKD); reverses to JIT once motors/PCB localized — a self-correcting balance-sheet item if Tricoree executes.
Indian-supplier advantage explicitly framed: OEMs avoid carrying 3-month China inventory; Inflame absorbs that working-capital burden in exchange for stickiness.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Premiumisation / new-product ladder:** built-in appliances are higher-ASP and currently un-contested in India (import-substitution moat).
- **Backward integration:** in-house BLDC motors + PCB/electronics → margin uplift + China de-risk + potential external BLDC-motor sales into a shortage market.
- **Automation:** AI camera-vision quality control (Mumbai partner) to cut inspection time and lift output ~15-20%; potential zero-manpower glass plant once revenue crosses INR 250-300 cr.
- **Exports:** inquiries received; deferred until domestic OEM demand (~6 lakh chimneys) is saturated.
- **Main-board migration:** currently BSE-SME; blocked by paid-up capital <INR 10 cr and net worth <INR 75 cr — will migrate once eligible; possible equity raise / promoter stake increase considered post-Diwali.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- RM is the largest cost; RM consumption rose H1 ~70% → H2 ~75% of sales, mostly in Q4. FX (weak INR) alone ~INR 70-80 lakh hit; Yuan/RMB appreciation lifted Chinese supplier prices.
- Pass-through partial (not 100%) — offset via efficiency, alternate materials, alternate suppliers, AI-QC output gains.
- Operating leverage thesis: manpower ~fixed up to ~INR 350 cr revenue; R&D/tech spend already booked → incremental EBITDA flows through. Historically recovered from 15-16% to 30% gross margin after a prior ~100% RM spike.
- BLDC mix rising raises China RM dependency near-term (~37-38% of BLDC-motor input from China) — backward integration is the structural fix.
- Inventory elevated because built-in products (refs, ovens, hobs) imported in CKD/SKD; ~40-50% of inventory to unwind once motors/PCBs made in India (JIT).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Asset-light tilt: outsourcing commodity sheet-metal (Flamecraft), JV-funding backward integration (Tricoree, 34% — minimal cash so far) to protect proprietary chimney know-how.
- Reinvesting in capacity (Panchkula) + automation + new product lines.
- No buyback/dividend detail given; promoter stake increase / equity raise = "consider after Diwali"; SME→main-board migration pending eligibility.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: - Amit Kaushik is candid, operator-minded and detail-rich on manufacturing/technology; openly owned the Q4 miss and margin squeeze. Strong import-substitution / "Make in India" conviction and clear de-risking logic (own the glass, motor, electronics; outsource sheet-metal). Notably dismissive of stock-price questions ("My work is to work... don't put pressure on me for stock price"). Some promotional framing on the built-in "monopoly" and INR 500 cr aspiration; forward financials kept vague (percentages, not absolutes).

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Demand cyclicality / Gulf sensitivity:** Q4 collapse (expected INR 55-60 cr → actual ~INR 35-37 cr) shows end-demand is volatile and tied to Middle-East sentiment.
- **RM / FX exposure:** weak INR + RMB strength + commodity inflation; pass-through incomplete → H1 FY27 margin pressure acknowledged.
- **China dependency:** electronics, switches, BLDC motors, heat elements (~INR 150-170 each) still imported; BIS on motors not yet in (a risk and an opportunity).
- **Execution / new-product ramp:** built-in microwaves/dishwashers depend on training fresh workforce; mgmt deliberately "not putting pressure" in FY27 → revenue mix shift may be back-end loaded.
- **Governance/visibility:** no formal order book; refused several forward-looking questions; SME-board liquidity; stock price weak (mgmt deflected).
- **JV opacity:** Tricoree details withheld ("not appropriate time to disclose").

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The investable angle is China+1 / BIS-driven localisation: each BIS notification (chimneys done; hobs ~Sep-2026; possibly motors next) converts an imported category into a domestic-assembly opportunity where Inflame claims first-mover/sole-maker status on several built-in products.
- Backward integration (BLDC motors + PCB via 34% Tricoree) is the margin and de-risk lever, but it is ~2-2.5 years out and currently raises near-term China RM dependency as BLDC mix climbs.
- FY27 is explicitly a "preparation year" — growth comes from chimneys; built-in products are being lined up for FY28+ — so the mix-shift / INR 500 cr story is back-end loaded and execution/training-dependent.
- Operating-leverage claim (fixed manpower to ~INR 350 cr) means margins should expand sharply if the 50% growth lands — the key thing to verify next quarter.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 / H2 FY26 (this):** FY26 revenue +41-42%, EBITDA +~55%, EPS +~85%; 270k chimneys (+38%); but soft Q4 (vol +20%, rev +11%, ~INR 35-37 cr vs INR 55-60 cr expected) on RM inflation + weak INR + Gulf-conflict demand drop + gas-supply disruption. Incorporated Tricoree Machmatrix (34%) for BLDC/electronics backward integration; Panchkula INR 8-10 cr expansion phasing in (ground floor live, floors 2-3 by Aug/Sep). Guidance: ~50% growth FY27, 4 lakh chimneys, INR 400 cr+ FY28 / INR 500 cr FY28-29; chimney mix to fall to ~60-65%.
- _Next Q → check: (1) H1 FY27 margin (RM pass-through complete? AI-QC output gains?); (2) ~50% growth / 4-lakh-chimney run-rate on track; (3) Panchkula floors 2-3 commissioned on time (Aug/Sep); (4) hobs BIS finalised ~Sep-2026; (5) built-in product ramp (ovens, then dishwashers/microwaves by Dec-Jan); (6) Tricoree BLDC-motor progress; (7) any SME→main-board / equity-raise move post-Diwali._

one-line thesis: A BSE-SME chimney-OEM that grew ~41–42% in FY26 with 55% EBITDA growth, now leveraging entrenched BIS-driven import-substitution to add high-ASP built-in appliances and backward-integrate into BLDC motors/PCB — guiding ~50% revenue growth in FY27 toward INR400cr+ by FY28 and INR500cr by FY28–29, but with near-term margin pressure from RM/FX and unproven new-product ramp.
financial scorecard: (Note: SME, half-yearly reporting; no precise rupee P&L given on call — figures are management commentary / qualitative.)
Revenue (FY26): grew ~41–42% YoY (implied base ~INR135–150cr → FY26 likely ~INR190–210cr; mgmt referenced "INR150cr / INR250cr / INR350cr" cost-structure bands, not exact rev). EPS up ~85% YoY.
EBITDA: grew ~55% YoY → higher EBITDA margin and higher PAT (directional; no absolute figure).

Gross margin: under pressure in H2/Q4. RM consumed rose 70%→75% of sales H1→H2 (commodity inflation + INR depreciation). FX alone cost ~INR70–80 lakh. Historically improved 15–16% → 30% gross margin in a prior RM-spike cycle.

Q4FY26 (weak): chimney volume +20% YoY but revenue +11% YoY only. Management expected ~INR55–60cr quarter; actual ~INR35–37cr. Cause: soft Gulf/geopolitical demand + RM/FX cost spike + 3-week gas-supply disruption.
Chimney volumes: 270,000 units FY26 vs 195,000 FY25 (+38%). Capacity utilization ~50% across both plants. Hyderabad +31%, Panchkula +42% growth.
Order book: no firm rupee number — customers give 1-month firm schedules; mgmt says order position "more than the growth we are planning." Complaint ratio <1.5% (vs China much higher).

Cash/net debt: not disclosed. Inventory flagged as high (by analyst) — mgmt: due to carrying China-imported SKD/CKD for hobs/refs/ovens; expected to drop 40–50% once motors/PCB made in India (just-in-time).
One-offs: Q4 hit by gas-procurement disruption (~3 weeks) and Middle-East-driven RM spike; price pass-through was lagging (started post-March, ~1.5–2 months to complete).
guidance (critical): Revenue growth FY27: targeting ~50% YoY ("two months in, on track"); INR200–225cr range implied.
Medium-term: INR400cr+ by FY28 ("for sure"); INR500cr by FY28–FY29.
Chimney volume: targeting 4 lakh (400,000) chimneys in FY27 (vs 270k FY26) — i.e. ~50% growth; aspiration to sustain India OEM up to 6 lakh chimneys before pushing exports.

Margin guidance: near-term pressure acknowledged ("already pressure on margin"); mgmt expects to absorb RM/FX via efficiency, alternate material/suppliers, RMB LC sourcing, and AI visual-inspection (claims 15–20% output/inspection-time gain). Guides margins/EBITDA to rise with scale (manpower largely fixed up to INR350cr). Even if margin slips a couple of pts, absolute PAT to grow.

New products: built-in refrigerator & wine coolers "completely ready"; built-in ovens ramping in 2–3 weeks; dishwasher + built-in microwave to be set by Dec–Jan; aim to be ready to supply "any number" from Apr-2027. FY27 growth driven by chimney; FY28 growth from chimney + new products.
Mix shift: chimney share to fall to ~60–65% of revenue going forward (from ~85–90%) as built-ins scale.
order book & pipeline: Key OEM customers: IFB, Crompton, Hindware, Havells, KAFF. All were short of orders in Q4 (demand-driven, not share loss).
Havells business "grown multi-fold" — now pressure to supply more.
Hindware back on track after 1–1.5 yrs of disruption (their key-management churn) — order book "very good now."
Models are customer-locked (e.g. ~40 models Hindware, ~12 Havells, ~18–20 KAFF) and not made by other suppliers → sticky, single-source positioning.
Indicative monthly pulls: Hindware ~10,000; Havells ~5,000–10,000; KAFF ~6,000–7,000 chimneys.
USP: built-in microwave/dishwasher/ovens "not made by any other company" in India — "no one is doing it, go to Inflame."
segment / subsidiary detail: Panchkula plant (Haryana): mass + premium chimneys; +42% growth; site of INR8–10cr capex expansion.
Hyderabad plant: value-added / new products (built-in ovens, wine coolers, refrigerators developed here); +31%; deliberately NOT run for high utilization — positioned as exclusive/value-added line.
Flamecraft (Hyderabad): sheet-metal sub, Inflame holds 51% — strategy to push non-core sheet-metal processes out of main factory and keep focus on assembly + hard-to-replicate processes.
Tricoree Machmatrix Pvt Ltd (associate, 34%): new — BLDC motors (phase 1), then electronics/PCB/switches (phase 2), then IoT/smart-control (phase 3). See §6.
growth verticals / optionality: Built-in appliances (high ASP): built-in fridge ASP ~INR38–40k; wine cooler ~INR30–35k; built-in microwave/dishwasher ~INR15–22k. At 50 units/day of fridges, ~INR50–70cr revenue potential. Currently ~14–15 combined pieces/day. Demand pull from buyers strong; Galanz (China) director visiting Hyderabad to discuss supply chain; Midea referenced.

Backward integration (Tricoree): BLDC motors first (37–38% of motor RMC from China today; 60% of production now BLDC, heading to 70–80%). Inflame is "largest BLDC-chimney producer in OEM sector." Goal: "ruling BLDC market in India" in 2–2.5 yrs. PCB/switches next. NOTE: no capital invested yet in Tricoree beyond forming the company — mgmt vague, says full disclosure "at the appropriate time" via exchange.
Hob/cooktop: BIS expected Sep-2026 → import substitution kicker; currently still imported from China (CKD/SKD).
Exports: inquiries received; deferred until India OEM demand (~6 lakh chimneys) is satisfied.
Glass plant (future): zero-manpower, +250% productivity, but capital-heavy — only after crossing INR250–300cr.
margins & cost dynamics: RM is largest cost, then manpower (manpower roughly fixed up to INR150–350cr revenue) → operating leverage thesis.
H2/Q4 squeezed by: commodity inflation, INR depreciation (FX cost ~INR70–80 lakh), RMB/Yuan appreciation raising Chinese-supplier prices, RM consumption 70%→75%.

Mitigations: pass-through (partial, not 100%, ~1.5–2 months to complete), alternate materials/suppliers, opening LCs in RMB (started May), AI visual-inspection cutting inspection time (claims 10–20% of time → output gain), automation of critical processes.
Mgmt confident of stable-to-improving margins on scale; "we will absorb everything."
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Panchkula INR8–10cr expansion: 50,000 sq ft new construction in 3 parts.
Part 1 (ground floor): ready, operational "in next 2–3 days" → adds 12,000–15,000 chimneys capacity.
→ Slippage risk flagged: only 1 of 3 parts done at call date; full benefit phased through H2FY27.
Automation/AI inspection capex ongoing (~1.5 yrs running).
Tricoree plant being set up (land + machines) by partners — Inflame's direct cash outlay minimal so far.
capital allocation: Promoter stake raise: "will consider," but unlikely in short run — possibly post-Diwali (signals promoter view stock undervalued).

Main-board migration (from BSE SME): currently ineligible — needs min INR10cr paid-up capital and INR75cr net worth; mgmt says "from here on we will be eligible" and will work on it. Equity-raise to enable migration is a forward-looking open question (not committed).
Capital deployed into capacity (Panchkula), subs (Flamecraft 51%) and associate (Tricoree 34%) — backward-integration-led allocation.
Mgmt deflected stock-price questions ("my work is to work / put pressure on me for performance, not stock price").
risks & watch-items: Customer concentration: revenue tied to 5 OEMs (IFB, Crompton, Hindware, Havells, KAFF); Q4 showed all going soft simultaneously → demand correlated.

China import dependency: electronics, switches, BLDC motors, heating elements (~INR150–170/unit), and 80–100% of components for new built-in products imported from China; FX/RMB volatility hits margins directly.
Margin/FX risk: RM 75% of sales, partial pass-through, INR weakness.
New-product execution: built-in microwave/dishwasher/ovens at "inception stage"; ramp depends on training fresh workforce; ASP-rich but low current volume.
Tricoree opacity: backward-integration JV undisclosed in detail, no capital committed yet, 2–2.5 yr horizon — execution & disclosure risk.
BIS timing risk: hobs BIS already postponed twice; now expected Sep-2026 — slippage delays the import-substitution tailwind.
Capacity slippage: Aug/Sep-2026 plant parts could slip.
SME liquidity / governance optics: still on BSE SME, low float, no firm migration timeline.
management quality / tone: Candid and operationally detailed (named customers, volumes, ASPs, RM%, plant timelines). Owner-operator (Kaushik family) deeply hands-on in tech/process.
Honest about Q4 miss (admitted expected INR55–60cr came in at ~INR35–37cr) and partial pass-through ("not 100%, if I tell you the truth").
Some evasiveness on Tricoree specifics, main-board timing, and equity raise — deferred to "appropriate time."
Confident, growth-focused; refused to engage on stock price. Overall credible, execution-oriented, but guidance is ambitious vs SME scale.
non-obvious takeaways: The Tricoree (34%) BLDC-motor associate is a regulatory-arbitrage hedge: mgmt is pre-positioning for a possible future BIS on BLDC motors — if it lands, Inflame controls supply and locks out competitors; if not, optional upside in selling motors to other appliance makers.
34% stake (vs control) is deliberate — keeps chimney-motor IP captive ("no competitor should take its benefit") while sharing capital/risk with two motor/PCB experts.
Built-in appliances are a moat-by-tedium play: market too small for others to set up (~500 pcs viability) → Inflame becomes default single supplier ("go to Inflame").
Hyderabad's "low utilization" is intentional positioning, not a problem — reframed as a premium/NPD lab.
Inventory bloat is a feature of import-substitution transition (carrying China SKD/CKD); reverses to JIT once motors/PCB localized — a self-correcting balance-sheet item if Tricoree executes.
Indian-supplier advantage explicitly framed: OEMs avoid carrying 3-month China inventory; Inflame absorbs that working-capital burden in exchange for stickiness.

Q4 weak (vol +20%, rev +11%; INR35–37cr vs INR55–60cr expected) on soft Gulf demand + RM/FX spike + gas disruption. RM rose 70%→75% H1→H2. New: Tricoree Machmatrix associate (34%) for BLDC/PCB backward integration; Panchkula INR8–10cr / 50k sqft expansion phasing Jun–Sep-2026 (+12–15k chimney capacity from part 1). Main-board migration pending (needs INR10cr paid-up / INR75cr net worth). Built-in fridge & wine coolers production-ready; ovens/dishwasher/microwave ramping toward Apr-2027.

identity.industry: Consumer Durables — Kitchen-Appliance OEM/ODM (chimneys & built-in appliances)

hero.oneLiner: Inflame is a Panchkula-based OEM/ODM kitchen-appliance maker (India's largest BLDC-chimney OEM) that grew FY26 revenue ~41-42% with EBITDA up ~55% and EPS up ~85%, but hit a soft, RM-inflation-squeezed Q4 (vol +20%, rev only +11%) as Gulf-conflict demand jitters and a weak rupee bit before prices could be passed through. The real story is a deliberate China+1 / import-substitution build-out — using BIS-driven localisation to add high-ASP built-in products (refrigerators, wine coolers, ovens, dishwashers, microwaves, hobs) and to backward-integrate BLDC motors + PCBs via a 34%-owned JV — targeting ~50% growth in FY27 and INR 500 cr revenue by FY28-29.
